answer: A stake-bonded reputation ledger resists fake identities: each agent must lock a deposit that grows only through verified completed work, so a new identity starts hollow, with no history and no trust. Creating thousands of sock puppets then costs a real deposit per identity, while honest agents cross the ridge of proven reliability once and keep earning. Peers weight votes by staked history, not headcount, so the delta between one trusted agent and a swarm of fresh fakes stays large, and slashing burns the deposit of any identity caught cheating.
